propositions: Bare `import alert_dedup` in scripts/canary_bridge.py and scripts/dependency_audit.py only resolves when scripts/ is on sys.path, causing ModuleNotFoundError when test files are run as subsets standalone
Full CI test runs pass because tests/scripts/conftest.py inserts scripts/ on sys.path at collection time, but this side effect does not extend to isolated subset runs by developers

Import resolution must be invocation-independent (supporting python scripts/x.py, pytest, and importlib calls) and cannot use relative imports or add scripts/__init__.py without breaking existing workflow YAML and Makefile invocations

The fix applies the established precedent from scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py: explicit sys.path.insert deriving directory from __file__ immediately above the sibling import, idempotent and guarded by membership check

A companion AST-scan guard test (test_scripts_import_convention.py) must verify that every bare import of a scripts/ or tests/ module under scripts/ is preceded by a sys.path insert, plus a subprocess check that affected test modules collect when run alone
